title: SYSK Selects: How Ouija Boards Work
summary: Rerun (SYSK Selects) of the Ouija board episode. The hosts trace the Ouija board from its mid-nineteenth-century spiritualism roots and the Kennard/Fuld/Parker Brothers lineage, describe the planchette and how to use the board, explain the ideomotor effect (with Chevreul's pendulum and facilitated communication as related examples), recount several Ouija-linked stories (the Kansas City Herd killing, El Cerrito mass hysteria, Sax Rohmer's Fu Manchu), and close with a listener mail story about a crack baby.

segments.title: Opening banter and Ouija teaser
segments.summary: Josh introduces the Selects episode and the hosts banter about the murder room office move, pronunciation of Wegia/Ouija, and The Exorcist.

segments.title: Origins and history of the Ouija board
segments.summary: The board's mid-nineteenth-century origins in spiritualism, claims of ancient origins with no evidence, Elijah Bond's patent and rival swastika board, Charles Kennard's naming story, and William Fuld's marketing and the sale to Parker Brothers, now Hasbro.

segments.title: Seances, mediums and the planchette
segments.summary: Seances and mediums in nineteenth-century America, earlier talking devices such as the dial plate, alphabet board and planchette with pencil, and the Ouija board's shift from mediums to home parlor game.

segments.title: How to use a Ouija board
segments.summary: Describes the board layout, yes/no corners, goodbye, the planchette's viewing window, gameplay with two or more players, tips on concentration, lighting, and ending the session with goodbye.

segments.title: Ideomotor effect and the science of planchette movement
segments.summary: Explains idiomotion and the ideomotor effect: unconscious muscle movement that moves the planchette, with the Chevreul pendulum example, facilitated communication as a controversial parallel, and a University of British Columbia study on blindfolded players.

segments.title: Ouija board stories
segments.summary: Stories of Ouija-linked events: the Kansas City Herd killing after a board message about infidelity, the El Cerrito mass hysteria, Sax Rohmer's Fu Manchu inspiration, and a suggested blindfold test to debunk the board.

segments.title: Listener mail: crack baby
segments.summary: A listener from Austin, Texas, Jim, describes calming a crack-exposed baby in a children's hospital neonatal unit around 2001.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts recommend the Museum of Talking Boards and HowStuffWorks article, invite listener stories, and sign off.
